analysis: The frame hasn't changed 2.5 hours into the session: bonds are still in charge. Indexes opened higher then rolled over after the data (ISM 54.5, prices paid 77.9, strong construction spending) — 'good economy' is 'bad for bonds' this week, and the 10Y pushed to ~5.34%. The prices-paid jump to 77.9 matters more than the headline PMI miss (54.5 vs 55.0 expected): it undercuts the 'inflation is handled' reading of yesterday's PCE and keeps October hike odds alive into Friday's NFP. On the stock side, the AI-capex paper trail keeps getting signed (Oracle/Tencent $7B chip lease, though single-source and unconfirmed) while signed domestic deals (SNPS, CEG, ACN +18% record day) are what the market is rewarding. Meta keeps bleeding relative to the Mag 7 on the OpenAI Dots-vs-Muse threat — yesterday's story, but still the reason META is the day's weak link. Signal vs noise: ISM prices-paid and tomorrow's jobs report are the signal; the South Korea LNG dispute is political noise (watch US LNG names only if it escalates); Alphabet's Gemini Argon price-war is signal for AI infrastructure pricing, the HN dev thread confirms the community is watching price, not just benchmarks.

community_signals.takeaway: Still front-page; dev commentary now centers on the pricing angle (Argon at ~one-fifth of GPT-6 Astra rates) and skepticism about the Fairwind-gated rollout speed, plus a mid-September Ask HN about Google sunsetting 2.5 Pro before a GA Pro replacement exists — reinforcing that the 'price war vs capability' question is what the bid in GOOGL trades on.

headlines.headline: Stocks reversed into the red after upbeat morning data: Dow -0.5% (~-225 pts), S&P 500 -0.2%, Nasdaq -0.1% in late-morning trading. August construction spending came in much stronger than expected, and the September ISM manufacturing PMI landed at 54.5 (vs 55.0 expected, 54.6 in August) with prices paid jumping to 77.9 from 71.1 — the strongest inflation read at the factory gate in months. The 10Y Treasury pushed to ~5.34%, toward a fresh 24-year high (~5.35% touched earlier), while the 2Y slipped to 4.87%. Only about 163 S&P 500 stocks were rising; only energy and tech sectors were green.
headlines.why_it_matters: Good news on the economy is bad news for bonds this week: the stronger data and the prices-paid spike re-anchor October rate-hike odds and keep the growth-vs-rates framing in charge — the higher open faded on the same bond tape as the morning briefs.

headlines.headline: Oil extended its rally: WTI +2.3% to ~$92.50 and front-month Brent +3.6% to ~$101.60 after Reuters reported Chinese refiners suspended October fuel exports to prioritize domestic supply; WSJ noted Brent briefly held above $100. Separately, South Korea's Industry Ministry formally objected to a White House claim of a $54B commitment to the Alaska LNG project, saying no final agreement has been reached.
headlines.why_it_matters: Rising energy prices are the second leg of the yield story (higher oil feeds inflation expectations and keeps the 10Y bid); the South Korea LNG pushback is political noise for now, only relevant to US LNG names if it escalates.

headlines.headline: Oracle (ORCL) rose ~2% premarket after the FT reported Tencent signed a ~$7B five-year lease for about 100,000 AI chips across Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia, with ~30% paid upfront — Tencent's largest overseas compute deal. The chips never enter China, using the export-rule distinction that allows leasing foreign compute capacity but not purchase. Reuters said it could not independently verify the report; neither company has confirmed.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile. If true, it's another multi-year signed AI-capex commitment for Oracle, whose shares are down over 50% from last September's highs on balance-sheet and spending worries; the read-through is continued AI chip demand (NVDA-class hardware) even in China-facing business.

headlines.headline: Meta (META) is again the Mag 7 laggard (down >1% vs small gains elsewhere), continuing Wednesday's weakness after OpenAI launched its Dots AI agent — investors see it as a threat to Meta's fast-growing Muse platform. StoneX's Mark Zgutowicz warned Meta's muse could intensify capex-spending worries rather than ease them; the stock is up over 28% in the past month on Muse enthusiasm.
headlines.why_it_matters: Explains META's divergence from the group: the bid in Meta is priced for AI-agent leadership, and a credible competitor agent launch reprices that — competitive-threat discount, not a fundamentals change.

headlines.headline: Accenture (ACN) +18%, on track for its largest percentage gain on record (data back to 2001), after fiscal Q4 beat: EPS $3.29 vs $3.18 expected, sales $19B (~$1B above views), bookings $22B vs ~$20B expected; shares cleared the 200-day moving average. IBM +3%, Cognizant +11% on the read-through. McCormick (MKC) -3.5%; Micron (MU) -1.5% as the sell-the-beat continued.
headlines.why_it_matters: Enterprise AI-demand signal beyond chips: record day on services names tied to AI implementation spend, not just the hardware chain.

headlines.headline: Nike (NKE) reports fiscal Q1 after today's close, stock up slightly at ~$35.40 near its lowest since early 2014 (down ~44% YTD). Street expects ~$11.35B revenue (-3% y/y) and $0.44 EPS; short interest at a record ~87M shares (~7% of float). Jefferies expects ~$11.5B revenue and $0.48 EPS, above consensus.
headlines.why_it_matters: Low bar plus record short interest makes this a squeeze-or-slap event after the close — the trade is China demand and margins, not the quarter's revenue line.
